summary: Feed s136_double is degraded: 58.6% of traffic is VXLAN-encapsulated and 14.5% of frames are sliced to 256 bytes. Both prevent this NDR (needs full payload, 9216B MTU) from inspecting inner payloads and detecting threats.

findings.root_cause: Packet broker is forwarding overlay traffic without VXLAN header stripping. 1770/3018 frames still encapsulated, indicating the broker has no strip/de-encapsulation policy for this VXLAN segment.
findings.impact_on_tool: NDR sees only outer VXLAN/UDP/IP headers, not inner Ethernet/IP and L7 payload. Flow correlation, lateral-movement detection and signature matching fail on 58.6% of traffic.

recommended_fix.why: Strip VXLAN headers at the packet broker and forward only the inner packets so the NDR can parse true endpoints and payloads for detection.

findings.root_cause: Packet broker slicing (snaplen) is set to ~256 bytes to save bandwidth/tool capacity. 437/3018 frames (14.5%) are cut short, well above 5% threshold.
findings.impact_on_tool: NDR needs full payload for DPI, file extraction and anomaly detection. Sliced frames lose application payload, breaking detection of C2, exploits and data exfiltration.

recommended_fix.why: Disable slicing or raise snaplen to the NDR's max 9216B so full packets/payloads are delivered for complete analysis.
